Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Honolulu HI
350 PM HST Wed Jul 29 2026

.SYNOPSIS...

The remnants of Fausto will continue to pass Hawaii to the north 
resulting in light winds and muggy conditions. Trades will 
quickly fill in tonight through early next week, becoming breezy 
to locally strong Friday into Saturday. Trades will ease to more 
typically breezy speeds early next week as the high weakens. 


&&

.DISCUSSION...
The remnant low of Fausto, roughly 160 miles north of Oahu, will 
continue to weaken while tracking west- northwest, north of the 
state. This low will continue keep light and variable winds 
across the state through tonight. A trailing cloud band with 
embedded light to locally heavy showers is currently moving from 
east to west across the Big Island. Elsewhere, the combination of 
light northerly winds and seabreezes is producing cloudy 
conditions with some embedded light showers along mountain slopes
and over interior areas. Rainfall rates are less than .1 inches 
per hour with higher rates of .5 inches in some of the brief heavy
showers. The band of scattered clouds and enhanced moisture will 
continue to move westward across the rest of the state tonight and
through the morning hours Thursday, increasing chances of 
showers. So far the small areas of heavy showers have been brief 
and not causing any flooding concerns. 

Thursday, a strong high will develop far northeast of the state 
allowing breezy to locally strong winds to return by Friday and 
Saturday.  Expect a more typical tradewind pattern with showers 
focused mainly along windward and mauka areas. Drier air will also
filter allowing dewpoints to dip below 70 degrees by Friday.
Downslope winds under this drier and stable airmass could meet or
exceed wind advisory criteria. We will continue to monitor all
available guidance and observations. 

Sunday into early next week trades will weaken to moderate to
locally breezy levels as Hurricane Genevieve tracks far northeast
of the state, disrupting the trade wind flow. 


&&

.AVIATION...
Variable afternoon winds will be replaced by east to southeast 
flow overnight as the remnants of former tropical cyclone Fausto 
pass north of Kauai. The east-southeast winds will spread over 
the Big Island late this afternoon and push a shallow band of 
moisture onto windward slopes. This moisture will produce MVFR 
ceilings on windward Big Island, where AIRMET Sierra for mountain 
obscuration may be needed through the evening. AIRMET Sierra 
remains posted for northern slopes of Maui and Molokai due to 
stubborn low ceilings in the high humidity conditions south of 
Fausto. Some improvement is expected late this afternoon, but the
AIRMET may be needed overnight for windward slopes as the 
moisture nearing the Big Island spreads westward. On Oahu and 
Kauai, ceilings over terrain should remain less extensive through 
most of the night.

Easterly trade winds will develop over the entire island chain
Thursday. Deeper moisture over the western end of the state may
produce widespread ceilings over windward slopes of Kauai and 
Oahu. VFR will prevail leeward.


&&

.MARINE...

Variable to light northerly winds today in response to Post-
Tropical Cyclone Fausto passing north of the islands. Trades
gradually build from east to west in its wake. Moderate to fresh
ESE trades become strong Friday through the weekend, eventually
warranting a Small Craft Advisory for winds, potentially as early
as tomorrow for the windier waters of Maui County and the Big
Island.

Nearshore PacIOOS buoys indicate continued decline in easterly
swell. The High Surf Advisory was cancelled earlier today. A 
small bump in short to medium period NE and N will arrive as Post-
Trop Cyclone Fausto advances westward north of the islands 
providing small surf along N facing shores. Flat to tiny surf then
returns by Thursday. Surf along E shores will trend up Thursday
night into the weekend due to a combination of building short 
period trade wind swell and renewed medium to long period E swell,
this time emanating from Hurricane Genevieve in the E Pac.

A medium period S swell building today and tonight will push 
S shore surf toward the summer average (5-6ft) for Thursday. Surf
then fades gradually through the weekend while a mix of small S 
swells maintains surf slightly below the seasonal average.


&&

.FIRE WEATHER...

Trade winds are expected to strengthen from east to west across
the state Thursday becoming breezy to locally strong Friday into
Saturday. As the winds become strong late Friday into Saturday, a
drier more stable airmass will filter in, increasing the 
potential for locally strong downsloping winds. While KBDI will 
remain below the critical thresholds there could still be some 
fire weather concerns. 

&&

.HFO WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
Small Craft Advisory until 6 AM HST Saturday for Pailolo Channel-
Alenuihaha Channel-Big Island Leeward Waters-Big Island 
Southeast Waters.


&&
